correctness.rationale: The support claim follows from \(|F(z)|\le |c|+u|z|\): invariance and repeated preimages of the tail beyond \(|c|/(1-u)\) force zero mass there. The pointwise identity \(|F(z)-c|=u|z|\), combined with invariance, gives equality of the complete radial pushforward laws. Taking second moments and completing the square yields \(E|Z-d|^2=\rho^2\), and the complex bias--variance identity gives \(V+|m-d|^2=\rho^2\). Boundary equality is equivalent to zero variance, hence to an invariant point mass, which is exactly a fixed-point atom. The exact verifier independently checks the rotation-norm identity and the standard \(c=1,u=9/10\) specialization.
